effect_estimate.comment: Descriptive bibliometric counts/percentages and qualitative realist synthesis are reported across the 63 included documents; no quantitative causal or regression effect estimate on water access or quality is estimated.
effect_estimate.value: Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported. Across 63 included documents (out of 279 reviewed), 71% were published after 2009, 24% (n = 15) had Indigenous first authors, 61% (n = 38) involved non-Indigenous researchers partnering with Indigenous communities, 26% focused on drinking water, 12% (n = 14) examined water governance, 35% explicitly used integrative Indigenous and Western approaches, and 40% (n = 25) acknowledged Aboriginal or treaty rights while 51% (n = 32) did not. The synthesis finds that top-down Western technocratic approaches and tokenistic add-on consultation fail to resolve Indigenous water inequities, whereas place-based co-management, equitable Indigenous participation throughout decision-making, institutional restructuring, and nation-to-nation governance are identified as promising for improving water management and drinking water quality, though direct community benefits were often difficult to discern in published reports.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 2, Abstract; PDF pp. 13–21, Findings; Box 2, PDF p. 21

mechanism_certainty.comment: Under CODEBOOK.md §9, systematic reviews appraised with AMSTAR 2 cannot exceed 2. Rated 1 because this secondary review synthesizes descriptive relationships across 63 studies regarding Indigenous participation, co-management, treaty rights, and institutional arrangements in water management and drinking water quality without direct primary observation of administrative processes at the point of household access, and explicitly notes that direct community water benefits were often difficult to discern from the published texts.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF pp. 16–21, Findings; PDF p. 24, Limitations

study_design.comment: Combined systematic review and realist review (SRR) of English-language peer-reviewed and grey literature published January 1979 to August 2015, guided by a National Advisory Committee and two national Water Gatherings (2014 and 2015) and coded with a 33-question realist reporting tool.
study_design.value: Systematic realist review of peer-reviewed and grey literature
